rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> 2-year RCBD field trial at Faridkot and Abohar (2019<U+2013>2020) with eight irrigation/fertigation treatments. Q2: Table 8 and 'Comparison of water use efficiency under SSDF vs surface flood' <U+2013> WUE 57.0% under surface flood versus 75.4<U+2013>83.5% under SSDF and 80.9% under SDI; irrigation water saved under SSDI 36<U+2013>61% (2019) and 20<U+2013>50% (2020) relative to flood (Tables 6, 7). Q4: Tables 6<U+2013>7 and 'Weather and site characteristics' / Conclusion <U+2013> drainage (~200<U+2013>300 mm) and runoff (86<U+2013>93 mm) under flood were far larger than under drip treatments, and the authors attribute the water saving to lesser drainage loss; soil profile moisture measured with TDR probe.
rows.notes: WUE and water saving derive from one method (soil-water-balance with metered irrigation and TDR soil moisture), so no triangulation. Only two sites (both sandy loam, same cultivar) and plot scale. No explicit limitation statement; deep-drainage assumptions and omission of upward flux are stated as methodological assumptions, not limitations. LSD values are given for BWP but no LSD, SD or CI for WUE; LSD is a significance threshold, not dispersion. The 80% ETc optimum is reported as a variation, not stated as a requirement.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own 2-year field experiment at two stations. Q2: Table 5 and Abstract/Conclusion <U+2013> SSDF at 80% ETc with 100% RDN gave 3,455 kg/ha seed cotton versus 2,728 kg/ha under surface flood, i.e. 26.6% higher; SSDI means at 80% and 100% ETc were 18.7% and 21.1% above flood. Q4: Table 5 and 'Yield attributes and seed cotton yield' <U+2013> bolls per plant were 23<U+2013>29% higher under SSDI than flood and identified as the primary reason for higher yield; Figure 4 shows a linear relationship between measured actual ET and seed cotton yield.
rows.notes: Yield measured by hand picking only (one method). Two sites, same crop and cultivar, plot scale. Authors note yield was lower at 60% ETc and that water and N 'govern' yield, but do not state an explicit requirement for the SSDF-over-flood effect; treated as a gradient, not a support factor. Table 5 reports LSD values only (significance threshold), no SD/SE/CI. No limitations of the result stated.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own field trial, Faridkot and Abohar, 2019<U+2013>2020, SSDI laterals buried at 20 cm. Q2: Tables 6<U+2013>7 and 'Effect of different treatments on water productivity indices' <U+2013> irrigation water applied under SSDI was 36<U+2013>54% (Faridkot) and 52<U+2013>61% (Abohar) lower than flood in 2019 and 20<U+2013>42% and 30<U+2013>50% lower in 2020, with WUE 75<U+2013>84% under SSDF versus 57% under flood (Table 8). Q4: Tables 6<U+2013>7 and Conclusion <U+2013> drainage and runoff under flood were several times those under SSDI; authors attribute savings to lesser drainage loss; soil moisture monitored by TDR profile probe.
rows.notes: Claim concerns SSDI water conservation, which the study tests directly against surface flood and surface drip. Single-method water-balance evidence, two sites, plot scale, no explicit limitations, no dispersion statistics for water saving or WUE (LSD only for BWP). Weed control (other part of the same passage) is handled in the companion row.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own 2-year field experiment on SSDF in cotton.
rows.notes: The study reports no data on weeds or weed control. It reports seed cotton yield, growth and yield attributes, actual ET, water productivity, WUE, NUE, fiber quality and economics for SSDF versus surface drip and surface flood. The weed-control claim is not supported by any result in this study.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Primary two-site, two-year field trial on cotton in Punjab, India. Data pooled across sites and years after Bartlett's test; only LSD values provided, no SD/SE/CI. No limitations section.
